tagline: A fast, minimalist web framework for Node.js, published as an npm package, with its own Mocha test suite and a large folder of runnable examples.

start_here.why: what Express is, installation and the quick-start example
the package entry point: it only re-exports ./lib/express
what index.js loads; the framework's real starting point
the scripts that run lint and the test suite, and the runtime dependencies
shows how the framework is exercised in tests: require the package, build an app, assert with supertest

diagrams.title: Express in context
diagrams.summary: Applications require the package, which loads its code from lib/ and relies on small npm dependencies. The repo also holds its own test suite and runnable examples, and GitHub Actions runs lint and tests.
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  app["Your Node.js app"] -->|"require('express')"| entry["index.js"]
  subgraph repo["This repository"]
    entry -->|"re-exports"| lib["lib/"]
    tests["test/ (Mocha + supertest)"] -->|"exercises"| entry
    examples["examples/"] -.->|"demonstrate"| lib
  end
  lib -->|"uses"| deps["npm dependencies (router, debug, accepts, ...)"]
  ci["GitHub Actions"] -->|"runs lint and tests"| tests
  ci -.->|"publishes"| npm["npm registry"]
diagrams.legend: Dashed lines are inferred from names, not from code that was read.

diagrams.title: Inside the package
diagrams.summary: index.js hands off to lib/express.js. The other files in lib/ are named for the pieces of an HTTP framework, but the links between them were not read.
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart TD
  idx["index.js"] --> exp["lib/express.js"]
  exp -.-> app["lib/application.js"]
  exp -.-> req["lib/request.js"]
  exp -.-> res["lib/response.js"]
  app -.-> view["lib/view.js"]
  app -.-> utils["lib/utils.js"]
diagrams.legend: Only index.js to lib/express.js was seen in code. Every dashed link is inferred from file names.

diagrams.title: What happens on npm test
diagrams.summary: The test script runs Mocha over test/ and test/acceptance/, loading test/support/env first, with leak checking on.
diagrams.mermaid:
sequenceDiagram
  participant D as Developer or CI
  participant N as npm test
  participant M as Mocha
  participant T as test/ and test/acceptance/
  participant E as index.js
  D->>N: npm test
  N->>M: mocha --require test/support/env --check-leaks
  M->>T: load spec files
  T->>E: require('..') and build an app
  T->>E: supertest request, assert response
  M-->>D: spec report

components.name: Test script
components.role: Defines the test, lint and coverage scripts

components.name: Acceptance tests
components.role: End-to-end style specs run in the same command

where_to_change.notes: Start from lib/express.js; roles of the other files are inferred.
test/app.js shows the pattern; remember --check-leaks fails tests that leak globals.
Each example is a folder; list it in examples/README.md.
Lint and tests run here; other workflows handle security scanning and publishing.

glossary.meaning: A test helper used in test/ to send HTTP requests to an app and assert on the response.
The specs under test/acceptance/, run together with the others by npm test.

gotchas: npm test runs Mocha with --check-leaks, so a test that creates a global variable will fail.
examples/ holds about 80 files, far more than lib/. Don't mistake it for the framework.
open_questions: What each file in lib/ does and how they depend on each other: only names were seen.
How routing is implemented: lib/ imports an external router package, but no routing code was read.
What legacy.yml and npm-publish.yml do exactly.
